I'm realizing the actual bug: replace_with_captures_at replaces all matches found in the extended subject, not just those within range, so for multiline text it ends up replacing matches beyond range.end too.

Let me examine replace_with_captures_at's implementation and compare it with find_iter_at_in_context to see how the range restriction is supposed to work.

I notice that find_iter_at_in_context properly bounds matches to the range by stopping when a match starts at or past range.end, but replace_all doesn't have this same safeguard—it calls replace_with_captures_at on the truncated subject without checking m.start() against range.end, so it could keep replacing matches beyond the intended range boundary.

I need to add a similar bound check to stop replacements after range.end, and also make sure dst only includes content up to range.end rather than the extra padding bytes used for lookahead. Let me check the replace_with_captures_at signature in the grep-matcher crate to figure out the right fix.

The fix is to avoid appending the extended portion directly and instead trim back to the actual range boundary before extending.

I need to implement my own loop using captures_iter_at that stops before range.end and only extends dst up to range.end for the trailing content, rather than relying on replace_with_captures_at's built-in tail append.

## Summary

The bug was in `Replacer::replace_all` in `crates/printer/src/util.rs`. For multi-line searches, the `subject` byte slice was intentionally extended past `range.end` (up to `MAX_LOOK_AHEAD` bytes) so the regex engine could satisfy look-ahead assertions. However, the code then called `matcher.replace_with_captures_at(subject, ...)`, whose default implementation unconditionally appends the entire remainder of `subject` after the last match (`dst.extend(&haystack[last_match..])`) — including all that extra look-ahead content that was never actually supposed to be part of the match's replacement output.

Fixed by replacing the call with a manual loop over `captures_iter_at` that mirrors the bounding logic already used in `find_iter_at_in_context`: it stops considering matches once they start at or beyond `range.end`, and only copies trailing non-matched bytes up to `range.end` (clamped to `subject.len()` to handle the line-terminator-trimming case in non-multiline mode).

Verified:
- `cargo test -p grep-printer` passes (94 passed, including all `replacement_*` tests).
- Manually reproduced the issue from the bug report and confirmed the `--replace` output now matches the non-replace output (single line), instead of leaking extra file content.

No tests, docs, or config were modified — only `crates/printer/src/util.rs`.
